extraction.Name: Angelina Roan Eagle, nee Shangreau
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent in fee to her 160 acre allotment at the time she got it; but she was advised by the Indian Agency that, if she did not take it, she would either have the accumulated taxes to pay on it, or, that it would finally be sold for taxes, as it had been reported to the tax collector, so she took it under protest
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged her allotment to a Mr. J Jordan, of Gordon, Nebraska, for $200.00; she could not keep up the payments on this mortgage, and, in 1923, Mr. L.D. Bailey, of Oelrichs, South Dakota, said he would pay the mortgage off, and get the land back for her
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to Mr. J Jordan of Gordon, Nebraska for $200.00; Mr. L.D. Bailey of Oelrichs, South Dakota paid off the mortgage and promised her $1000.00 for her allotment but only paid her $50.00 on two different occasions
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: got behind in taxes, about 1922; she could not keep up the payments on this mortgage
extraction.Occupation/Income: family is supported by her husband, who farms for a living, and works out some, too
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent, health good; mother of five small children, whose health is good; husband is not healthy, being somewhat bothered with tuberculosis; if he had actually paid the $1000.00 cash, it would not have been even a fair price for the allotment; she writes to Bailey about money due her, he makes appointments to meet payments but never keeps them; has never received any aid from the County, State or the United States Government; document sworn November 23, 1928; allotment is 160 acres
